units.text: INT. SEAGULL - CONTINUOUS
Ah, youth, youth!
units.name: DORN

units.text: It is always “Youth, youth,” when there is nothing else to be said.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: She takes snuff.
DORN takes the snuff-box out of her hands and flings it into the bushes.
Don’t do that, it is horrid.
units.name: DORN

units.text: A pause.
I hear music in the house. I must go in.
units.name: DORN

units.text: Wait a moment.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: What do you want?
units.name: DORN

units.text: Let me tell you again. I feel like talking.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: She grows more and more excited.

I do not love my father, but my heart turns to you. For some reason, I feel with all my soul that you are near to me. Help me! Help me, or I shall do something foolish and mock at my life, and ruin it. I am at the end of my strength.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: What is the matter? How can I help you?
units.name: DORN

units.text: I am in agony. No one, no one can imagine how I suffer.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: She lays her head on his shoulder and speaks softly.
I love Constantine.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Oh, how excitable you all are! And how much love there is about this lake of spells!
units.name: DORN

units.text: Tenderly.
But what can I do for you, my child? What? What?
units.name: DORN

units.text: The curtain falls.
The lawn in front of SORIN’S house.
The house stands in the background, on a broad terrace.
The lake, brightly reflecting the rays of the sun, lies to the left.
There are flower-beds here and there.
It is noon; the day is hot.
ARKADINA, DORN, and MASHA are sitting on a bench on the lawn, in the shade of an old linden.
An open book is lying on DORN’S knees .
To MASHA.
Come, get up.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: They both get up.
Stand beside me. You are twenty-two and I am almost twice your age. Tell me, Doctor, which of us is the younger looking?
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: You are, of course.
units.name: DORN

units.text: You see! Now why is it? Because I work; my heart and mind are always busy, whereas you never move off the same spot. You don’t live. It is a maxim of mine never to look into the future. I never admit the thought of old age or death, and just accept what comes to me.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: I feel as if I had been in the world a thousand years, and I trail my life behind me like an endless scarf. Often I have no desire to live at all. Of course that is foolish. One ought to pull oneself together and shake off such nonsense.
units.name: MASHA

units.text: Sings softly.
“Tell her, oh flowers--”

And then I keep myself as correct-looking as an Englishman. I am always well-groomed, as the saying is, and carefully dressed, with my hair neatly arranged. Do you think I should ever permit myself to leave the house half-dressed, with untidy hair? Certainly not! I have kept my looks by never letting myself slump as some women do.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She puts her arms akimbo, and walks up and down on the lawn.
See me, tripping on tiptoe like a fifteen-year-old girl.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: I see. Nevertheless, I shall continue my reading.
units.name: DORN

units.text: He takes up his book.
Let me see, we had come to the grain-dealer and the rats.
units.name: DORN

units.text: And the rats. Go on.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She sits down.
No, give me the book, it is my turn to read.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She takes the book and looks for the place.
And the rats. Ah, here it is.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: She reads.

“It is as dangerous for society to attract and indulge authors as it is for grain-dealers to raise rats in their granaries. Yet society loves authors. And so, when a woman has found one whom she wishes to make her own, she lays siege to him by indulging and flattering him.” That may be so in France, but it certainly is not so in Russia. We do not carry out a programme like that. With us, a woman is usually head over ears in love with an author before she attempts to lay siege to him. You have an example before your eyes, in me and Trigorin.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: SORIN comes in leaning on a cane, with NINA beside him.
MEDVIEDENKO follows, pushing an arm-chair.
In a caressing voice, as if speaking to a child.
So we are happy now, eh? We are enjoying ourselves to-day, are we? Father and stepmother have gone away to Tver, and we are free for three whole days!
units.name: SORIN
